ARE COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT MFA No.200251/2020 is filed by the insurer challenging the quantum of compensation awarded as well as 50% of the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation while MFA Crob.No.200011/2021 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and I Additional Sessions Judge, Raichur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.323/2016, vide judgment and award dated 13.12.2019.
2.
The claimant Nos.1, 2 and 5 are the wife and children of deceased Veeresh and claimant Nos.3 and 4 are his parents.

The claimants claimed that deceased was riding a moped and dashed against a parked tractor-trailer bearing registration No.KA-37/TA-3243 and KA-36/TA- 6184 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle').

The claimants contended that the deceased suffered injuries in NC:
2023:KHC-K:1273 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200011 of 2021 the accident and succumbed to the injuries in the hospital.

They claimed that the deceased was 28 years old and was earning Rs.2,00,000/- per annum from agriculture and Rs.2,00,000/- per annum from grocery business and was contributing and maintaining the family.
Therefore, they sought for compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the tractor-trailer.

sentences.text: The insurer of the offending vehicle contested the claim petition and contended that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the deceased.
It also claimed that the deceased did not possess a valid licence to ride a moped.
It claimed that the deceased dashed against a parked tractor-trailer and therefore he had contributed to the cause of the accident.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and she marked Exs.P1 to P9.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 to R3.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1273 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200011 of 2021 5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the deceased as well as driver of the offending vehicle had contributed to the accident in equal measure.

In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and deducted 1/4th towards personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:
Loss of dependency to all Rs.12,85,200/- petitioners Loss of love and affection, loss of Rs.70,000/- estate and funeral expenses to 1st petitioner Loss of love and affection to 2nd Rs.1,00,000/- and 5th petitioners Loss of filial consortium to 2nd Rs.80,000/- and 5th petitioner Loss of estate to 2nd and 5th Rs.30,000/- petitioner Loss of love and affection to 4th Rs.50,000/- petitioner Loss of filial consortium to 4th Rs.40,000/- petitioner Loss of estate to 4th petitioner Rs.15,000/-
Total Rs.16,70,200/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1273  C/W MFA.CROB No. 200011 of 2021 6.

The Tribunal directed the insurer of the tractor- trailer to pay 50% of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till its realization.
7. Being aggrieved by the negligence attributed to the driver of the tractor-trailer, the insurer is before this Court.
Likewise, the claimant has sought for enhancement of compensation.
8. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/insurer as well as the learned counsel for the cross objectors/claimants.
9. The accident involving the two vehicles is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the tractor-trailer was parked on the road which he could not have.

The fact that the accident happened United India vs Nirmala W/O Veeresh And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187441904/
5 at 11.00 a.m. makes it probable that the deceased while trying to overtake, must have been unnerved by another vehicle coming from the opposite direction and while trying to avert an accident, must have dashed against the parked tractor-trailer.

sentences.text: NC: 2023:KHC-K:1273 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200011 of 2021 10.
In that view of the matter, the deceased too was negligent as he did not exercise due care and caution and thereby had contributed to the accident.

Since the accident happened in the day time,
the deceased must have been careful after seeing the parked vehicle on the road.
The finding of the tribunal that the driver of the offending vehicle had contributed to the extent by 50% deserves to be revisited.
Having regard to the fact that the driver of the tractor-trailer parked it on the road, the negligence attributable to the driver of the offending vehicle is enhanced from 50% to 75%.

11. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month and must have factored loss of future prospects at 40%.

Likewise, claimant Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5 are entitled to loss of filial consortium due to the death of the deceased as held by the Apex court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1273 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200011 of 2021 ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

In that view of the matter, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation as follows:
Loss of dependency Rs.17,13,600/- Loss of spousal consortium to Rs.44,000/-
claimant No.1 Loss of parental consortium to Rs.88,000 Loss of filial consortium to Rs.88,000/-
Loss of estate Rs.33,000/-
Total Rs.19,66,600/-
12.

In view of the above, the appeal filed by the insurer is dismissed and the cross objection filed by the claimants is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.8,35,100/- determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.19,66,600/-.

The insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay 75% of the total compensation, which amounts to Rs.14,74,950/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of - 11 - United India vs Nirmala W/O Veeresh And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187441904/

The same shall be deposited before the Tribunal within one month.

Out of the compensation and interest, 30% each shall be kept in the name of claimant Nos.2 and 5 in any nationalized Bank for a period of 5 years or till they attain the age of majority, whichever is later.
The remaining 40% shall be released in favour of claimant Nos.1, 3 and 4 in equal portions.
Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the concerned Tribunal for necessary orders.
